passage: You missed an important lab session last Thursday because you were sick. Your chemistry professor, Dr. Patel, requires students to complete all lab sessions to pass the course.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Explain why you missed the lab session
• Ask whether you can make up the session
• Suggest when you are available
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Dr. Patel,

I am writing to explain why I was absent from last Thursday's lab session. I had a high fever and a bad cough, and my doctor advised me to stay home for two days. I have attached the note from the campus clinic.

I understand that every lab session is required to pass the course, so I would like to ask whether I could make up the missed experiment. If there is another section running the same lab this week, I would be happy to join it.

I am free on Monday and Wednesday afternoons, and on Friday morning before ten. I can also come in at another time if that is more convenient for the lab assistant.

Thank you for your understanding. I look forward to hearing from you.

Best regards,
Ken Tanaka

passage: Your study group booked a room in the library for a group project, but when you arrived the room had been given to another group. You want to write to the library services manager, Ms. Rivera.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Describe what happened
• Explain how this affected your group
• Suggest a way to prevent this problem in the future
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Ms. Rivera,

I am writing about a problem my study group experienced yesterday. We had reserved Room 214 from 3:00 to 5:00 p.m. through the online booking system, and I received a confirmation email. However, when we arrived, another group was using the room, and they also had a confirmation.

Because no other rooms were available, we had to work in the noisy main hall. We were preparing a presentation that is due on Friday, so losing two hours of practice time was a serious setback for us.

I wonder if the booking system could be updated so that it prevents two groups from reserving the same room at the same time. It might also help if staff at the front desk could check reservations when there is a conflict.

Thank you for looking into this matter.

Sincerely,
Maria Lopez

passage: Your friend Alex is visiting your city next month and has asked you for advice about what to do there. Alex loves food and history.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Recommend a place to visit
• Suggest a restaurant or food to try
• Offer to help with something during the visit
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Hi Alex,

I'm so happy you're coming next month! I've been thinking about what you might enjoy here.

Since you love history, you should definitely visit the old castle on the hill. It was built more than four hundred years ago, and there is a small museum inside that explains how people lived back then. The view from the top is amazing, too.

For food, you have to try the noodle shop near the central station. It's tiny and there is usually a line, but their spicy miso ramen is the best I've ever had. Go before noon if you want to avoid waiting.

If you like, I can pick you up at the airport and show you around on Saturday. Just send me your flight details when you have them.

See you soon,
Yuki

passage: You are the treasurer of a student club. The student activities office has announced that club budgets for next year will be cut by 30 percent. You want to write to the director, Mr. Okafor.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Explain what your club does
• Describe how the budget cut would affect your club
• Request a meeting to discuss the decision
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Mr. Okafor,

I am the treasurer of the Environmental Action Club, and I am writing about the recent announcement regarding next year's club budgets.

Our club organizes monthly campus clean-ups, runs a recycling workshop for first-year students, and invites two guest speakers each semester. Last year, more than three hundred students took part in our events.

A 30 percent cut would make it very difficult to continue these activities. In particular, we would no longer be able to pay travel costs for our speakers, and we might have to reduce the number of workshops by half.

I fully understand that the university faces financial pressure. However, I would appreciate the opportunity to meet with you to explain our situation in more detail and to discuss possible alternatives.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Daniel Kim

passage: You bought a desk lamp from an online store, but it arrived broken. You want to write to the store's customer service department.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Describe the product and the problem
• Explain what you would like the store to do
• Ask a question about the return process
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Customer Service Team,

I recently ordered a white LED desk lamp (order number 58213) from your website. It arrived yesterday, but unfortunately the lamp was damaged. The base was cracked, and the light does not turn on even when it is plugged in.

I would like to receive a replacement as soon as possible, because I need the lamp for studying. If a replacement is not available, I would prefer a full refund.

Could you please tell me how I should return the broken lamp? I would also like to know whether I need to pay for the shipping, and whether I should use the original box, which was also slightly damaged.

Thank you for your help. I look forward to your reply.

Kind regards,
Sara Ahmed

passage: You are taking an online course, and the instructor, Professor Lin, has asked students for feedback on the course halfway through the semester.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Mention something you have found helpful
• Describe a difficulty you have had
• Make a suggestion for improving the course
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Professor Lin,

Thank you for asking for our feedback on the course so far.

I have found the weekly video lectures very helpful. They are short and well organized, and the summary slides at the end make it easy to review the key concepts before each quiz.

One difficulty I have had is with the discussion board. Because many students post at the last minute, it is hard to have a real conversation, and some threads end up with forty replies that nobody has time to read.

I would suggest dividing the class into smaller discussion groups of about eight students and setting two deadlines: one for the first post and a later one for replies. I think this would encourage more meaningful exchanges.

Thank you again for your efforts in making this course engaging.

Best regards,
Lena Fischer

passage: Your neighbor, Mr. Hughes, often plays loud music late at night, and it is making it hard for you to sleep before your early classes.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Introduce yourself and explain the problem politely
• Explain why the problem matters to you
• Suggest a solution
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Mr. Hughes,

My name is Priya, and I live in Apartment 3B, directly below yours. I hope you don't mind me writing to you about something.

Over the past few weeks, I have often heard music from your apartment until around one or two in the morning. I'm sure you don't realize how much sound travels through the floor in this building.

The problem is that I have classes at eight o'clock four days a week, so I need to go to bed by eleven. Recently I've been feeling very tired during my morning lectures.

Would it be possible to turn the music down after eleven on weekdays? Weekends are no problem at all. I would really appreciate it, and please let me know if anything from my apartment ever bothers you, too.

Thank you,
Priya Sharma

passage: You want to apply for a summer research position in Dr. Morgan's psychology lab. You saw the announcement on the department website.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Explain why you are interested in the position
• Describe relevant experience or skills
• Ask about the next steps in the application process
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Dr. Morgan,

I am a second-year psychology major, and I am writing to express my interest in the summer research assistant position advertised on the department website.

I am particularly interested in your lab's work on sleep and memory. After taking your Cognitive Psychology course last semester, I became curious about how researchers design experiments that measure memory accurately.

Last year I volunteered at the campus counseling center, where I helped organize survey data in Excel. I have also completed an introductory statistics course and am currently learning to use R. I believe these skills would allow me to contribute to data collection and analysis.

Could you let me know what the next steps in the application process are? I would be happy to send my résumé and a writing sample.

Thank you for considering my application.

Sincerely,
Omar Haddad

passage: Your classmate Jordan was absent from yesterday's history class and has emailed you asking what happened.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Summarize what was covered in class
• Tell Jordan about an upcoming assignment
• Offer to share your notes
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Hi Jordan,

Sorry to hear you were sick! Here's what you missed yesterday.

Professor Grant talked about the causes of the Industrial Revolution in Britain. She focused on three main factors: the supply of coal, new farming methods that freed up workers, and the growth of trade with other countries. She also showed some interesting photos of early factories.

Also, she gave us a new assignment. We have to write a two-page response to the article on child labor, which is posted on the course website. It's due next Wednesday at the start of class.

If you want, I can scan my notes and send them to you tonight. They're a bit messy, but I wrote down most of the important points.

Feel better soon!
Chris

passage: You recently attended a career workshop organized by the university career center. The workshop leader, Ms. Grant, has asked participants to send comments.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Thank the organizer and mention what you learned
• Explain how you plan to use what you learned
• Suggest a topic for a future workshop
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Ms. Grant,

Thank you very much for organizing last Tuesday's workshop on job interviews. I found it extremely useful, especially the practice session in which we answered common questions and received feedback from a partner.

I learned that I tend to give answers that are too general. Your advice to use specific examples, structured as situation, action, and result, was very practical. I plan to prepare three or four such examples before my internship interviews next month.

For a future workshop, I would suggest a session on online interviews. Many companies now hold first-round interviews by video, and I think students would benefit from tips on lighting, camera position, and how to maintain eye contact through a screen.

Thank you again for your excellent work.

Best regards,
Tom Becker

passage: You have just moved into a university dormitory, and the heating in your room is not working. It is the middle of winter.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Describe the problem
• Explain how long it has been happening
• Ask when it can be repaired
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Housing Office,

My name is Lucas Silva, and I live in Room 412 of Maple Hall. I am writing to report a problem with the heating in my room.

The heater does not produce any warm air, even when I set the temperature to the highest level. It makes a quiet clicking noise, but the room stays very cold. At night the temperature inside is around twelve degrees.

I first noticed the problem four days ago, when I moved in. I thought it might start working after a while, but nothing has changed, and I have had to sleep in my coat.

Could you please let me know when a technician will be able to repair it? I am usually in my room after 4 p.m., but you are welcome to enter while I am out if necessary.

Thank you,
Lucas Silva

passage: You are organizing a conference for students in your department and would like a well-known local author, Ms. Chen, to give a talk.
question:

answer:
Dear Ms. Chen,

My name is Hana Ito, and I am a member of the organizing committee for the Westbrook University Student Literature Conference, which will be held on April 18.

We are writing to invite you to give the opening talk. Many of our students have read your novel The River Between, and it was discussed in two of our courses this year. We believe your experience of writing about immigrant families would be inspiring for students who hope to become writers themselves.

We would ask you to speak for about forty minutes, followed by a twenty-minute question-and-answer session. The talk would begin at 10 a.m. in the main auditorium, which seats about two hundred people. We would be able to cover your travel expenses and offer a modest speaking fee.

We would be honored if you could accept our invitation.

Sincerely,
Hana Ito

question:

answer:
Dear Mr. Davis,

I just saw the work schedule for next week, and I noticed that I am scheduled to work from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. on Thursday, December 12.

Unfortunately, I have my final exam in economics that day from 10 a.m. to noon. The exam date was set by the university, so I am not able to change it.

I have already talked to Emma, and she has kindly agreed to take my Thursday shift if I work her Saturday shift instead. If that is acceptable to you, we would just need you to update the schedule. Alternatively, I could work only from 1 p.m. to 3 p.m. on Thursday.

Thank you for your understanding. I really appreciate how flexible you have been with my class schedule this semester.

Best regards,
Mia Johnson

passage: You are a teaching assistant for an introductory biology course. Several students have told you that they find the weekly quizzes confusing. You want to write to the course professor, Dr. Wallace.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Describe the students' concern
• Give your own view of the problem
• Suggest a change
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Dr. Wallace,

I wanted to let you know about a concern several students raised during my office hours this week.

At least six students told me that they find some of the weekly quiz questions confusing. In particular, they said that questions with two negatives, such as "Which of the following is not unlikely," are hard to interpret, and they feel they lose points because of the wording rather than their understanding of the biology.

Having looked at the last two quizzes again, I think their concern is reasonable. Most students who missed those questions answered the related lab questions correctly.

Would you consider rewording questions that contain double negatives, or perhaps adding a short practice quiz at the start of the semester so students can get used to the format?

Please let me know if you would like me to help revise any questions.

Best,
Ryan Clark

passage: Your cousin Sam is starting university next year and has asked for your advice about choosing classes.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Give one piece of advice about choosing classes
• Share an experience from your first year
• Encourage Sam
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Hi Sam,

Congratulations on getting into university! I'm really excited for you.

My biggest piece of advice is not to take too many difficult classes in your first semester. Try to balance one or two challenging courses with some that you're simply interested in. That way, you'll have time to adjust to university life.

In my first year, I signed up for three science courses with labs at the same time. I thought I could handle it, but I was in the lab almost every afternoon, and I hardly had time to make friends or join any clubs. In my second semester I made a better mix, and I enjoyed it much more.

Don't worry too much, though. Everyone feels a little lost at first, and you'll figure it out quickly. Call me anytime if you have questions!

Love,
Jess

passage: The university is planning to replace a small park on campus with a new parking lot. The planning committee has invited students to send their opinions.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• State your opinion about the plan
• Give reasons for your opinion
• Suggest an alternative
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Members of the Planning Committee,

Thank you for inviting students to comment on the proposal to replace Oak Park with a parking lot. I would like to express my opposition to this plan.

Oak Park is one of the few green spaces on the east side of campus. On sunny days, dozens of students eat lunch there, and several classes use it for outdoor activities. It also provides shade and helps reduce heat around the nearby buildings in summer.

In addition, building more parking may encourage more people to drive, which seems to conflict with the university's goal of reducing carbon emissions.

As an alternative, I would suggest expanding the shuttle bus service from the train station or adding a second level to the existing parking garage on North Street. Either option would increase access without losing the park.

Sincerely,
Grace Wu

passage: You borrowed a camera from the media center for a class project, but you accidentally damaged the lens.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Explain what happened
• Apologize and take responsibility
• Ask what you should do next
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Media Center Staff,

I am writing about the camera I borrowed last Monday (equipment number C-207) for my documentary project.

While I was filming outdoors on Friday, I set the camera down on a bench, and it slid off and fell onto the pavement. The camera still turns on, but there is a crack across the front of the lens, and the pictures now have a blurry line.

I am very sorry about this. It was my mistake for not keeping the camera in its case, and I am prepared to pay for the repair or replacement.

Could you please tell me what I should do next? I can bring the camera back to the center tomorrow, and I would also like to know whether the repair cost will be added to my student account.

Sincerely,
Ahmed Nasser

passage: You read an article in the campus newspaper claiming that most students do not use the university gym. You disagree, and you want to write to the editor.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Explain what the article claimed
• Explain why you disagree
• Suggest what the newspaper could do
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Editor,

I am writing in response to last week's article, "Empty Gym, Wasted Money," which claimed that most students rarely use the university fitness center and that its budget should be reduced.

I disagree with this conclusion. The article was based on observations made between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m., when most students are in class. As someone who works part-time at the center, I can confirm that it is often so crowded in the early morning and evening that students have to wait for equipment. According to our entry records, more than four thousand students used the gym last month.

I would suggest that the newspaper publish a follow-up article using the center's full attendance data, and perhaps interview students who use it regularly. This would give readers a more accurate picture.

Sincerely,
Kevin Osei

passage: Your friend Mei invited you to her birthday party this Saturday, but you cannot go because of a family event.
question:

• Suggest another way to celebrate together
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Hi Mei,

Thanks so much for inviting me to your birthday party! It sounds like it's going to be a lot of fun.

Unfortunately, I won't be able to come. My grandparents are celebrating their fiftieth wedding anniversary this Saturday, and my whole family is traveling to their town for the weekend. I really can't miss it.

I feel bad about missing your party, though, so can I take you out for dinner next week instead? There's a new Korean barbecue place downtown that I've been wanting to try. How about Tuesday or Wednesday evening? It'll be my treat, of course.

I hope you have a wonderful birthday, and I can't wait to hear all about the party!

Hugs,
Lily

passage: You want to take an advanced seminar next semester, but you have not completed the required introductory course. You want to write to the seminar instructor, Professor Adams.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Explain your situation
• Describe why you think you are prepared for the seminar
• Ask for permission to enroll
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Professor Adams,

I am a third-year economics major, and I am very interested in enrolling in your seminar on behavioral economics next semester. However, I have not taken Economics 210, which is listed as a prerequisite.

I transferred from Riverside Community College last year, where I completed a course called Introduction to Decision Making. According to its syllabus, which I have attached, it covered most of the same topics, including prospect theory and risk preferences. I also received an A in Intermediate Microeconomics here last semester.

In addition, I have read Daniel Kahneman's Thinking, Fast and Slow and wrote a research paper on consumer decision making for another course.

Would you be willing to grant me permission to enroll in the seminar? I would be glad to meet with you during office hours to discuss my preparation.

Sincerely,
Isabel Reyes

Thank you,
Nora Bergman

passage: Your university is considering making all first-year students live on campus. The dean of students, Dr. Romero, has asked for student input.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• State whether you support the proposal
• Give at least one reason based on your own experience
• Mention a possible concern and how it could be addressed
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Dr. Romero,

Thank you for asking students for their views on requiring first-year students to live on campus. Overall, I support the proposal.

During my first year, I lived in a residence hall, and it made a huge difference to my adjustment. I met most of my closest friends there, and because the library and tutoring center were a five-minute walk away, I used them far more often than my friends who commuted.

However, one concern is cost. On-campus housing is more expensive than living with family, and some students may not be able to afford it. To address this, the university could offer housing scholarships or allow exemptions for students who live within a certain distance of campus.

I hope these comments are helpful.

Sincerely,
Ethan Brooks

• Explain why it would be a good choice
• Mention something members should prepare
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Hi Jamie,

Thanks for asking for our ideas about the next trip. I'd like to suggest Pine Ridge Trail in Clearwater State Park.

I think it would be a great choice for our group. It's only about an hour and a half by car, so we wouldn't need to leave too early. The trail is around eleven kilometers long and not too steep, which means our newer members could manage it. At the top, there's a lake where we could have lunch and take photos.

Members should bring good walking shoes, because parts of the trail can be muddy, especially in spring. It would also be a good idea to bring a light rain jacket, since the weather in the mountains changes quickly.

Let me know what you think!

Best,
Carlos

passage: You submitted a research paper for a class and received a lower grade than you expected. The comments said your argument was "unclear." You want to write to your instructor, Dr. Evans.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Explain why you are writing
• Ask for specific feedback
• Ask about opportunities to improve
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Dr. Evans,

Thank you for returning our research papers. I am writing because I would like to better understand the feedback on my paper about urban water policy.

I noticed that you described my argument as unclear. I was hoping you could point out which sections in particular caused confusion. For example, was the problem mainly in my thesis statement, or in how I connected the case studies to my main claim?

I take this feedback seriously, and I want to improve my writing for the final project. Would it be possible to meet during your office hours to discuss the paper? I would also like to know whether students are allowed to submit a revised version, or whether there are any resources, such as the writing center, that you would recommend.

Thank you for your time.

Sincerely,
Julia Novak

passage: Your roommate, Ben, is going away for the weekend and has asked you to take care of his cat.
question:

• Ask questions about how to care for the cat
• Mention a possible problem
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Hi Ben,

Of course I'm happy to look after Luna this weekend! You've helped me out plenty of times.

I just have a few questions. How much food should I give her, and how many times a day? Does she need any medicine, or is there anything she's not allowed to eat? Also, should I let her sleep in my room, or does she usually stay in yours?

One thing I should mention is that I have a study group on Saturday afternoon, so I'll be out from about one to six. Do you think she'll be OK alone for that long? If not, I could ask Kate to stop by and check on her.

Have a great trip, and don't worry about Luna!

Cheers,
Dan

answer:
Dear Library Volunteer Coordinator,

I saw your advertisement for after-school reading volunteers on the library's website, and I would like to apply.

I am a second-year education student at Lakeview University, and I hope to become an elementary school teacher. I have always loved reading, and I believe that helping children enjoy books is one of the most valuable things I could do in my free time.

Could you tell me which days and times volunteers are needed? I am available on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons after 3 p.m., and I could commit to at least one semester.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Emily Watson

passage: You work part-time at the university information desk. Your supervisor, Ms. Foster, has asked staff to suggest ways to improve service for international students.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Describe a problem international students often face
• Suggest a specific improvement
• Explain the benefits of your suggestion
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Ms. Foster,

Thank you for asking for our suggestions about serving international students more effectively.

One problem I notice almost every day is that new international students have difficulty finding offices across campus. Many of them are confused by building names that do not appear on the maps they downloaded, and some have walked for half an hour looking for the immigration advising office.

I would suggest creating a simple multilingual guide with photos of the main buildings and a list of where key services are located. We could also run short campus tours led by current international students during the first two weeks of each semester.

These measures would reduce the number of basic questions at our desk and help new students feel more confident and welcome. They might also improve the university's reputation among international applicants.

Best regards,
Aiko Mori

passage: You want to start a new student club on campus focused on sustainable living. To register a new club, you must write to the student activities office.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Describe the purpose of the club
• Explain why it would benefit students
• Ask what you need to do to register the club
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Student Activities Office,

I am writing to ask about registering a new student club called Green Living Collective.

The purpose of the club is to help students reduce waste and live more sustainably in their daily lives. We plan to hold monthly workshops on topics such as cooking with leftovers, repairing clothes, and saving energy in dorm rooms. We would also like to organize a clothing swap at the end of each semester.

I believe the club would benefit students in several ways. Many students want to live more sustainably but do not know where to start, and our activities would give them practical skills while also helping them save money. So far, twenty-three students have signed up to join.

Could you please tell me what documents are required to register the club and whether we need a faculty advisor?

Sincerely,
Liam O'Connor

Dear Student Activities Office,

I am writing to ask about registering a new student club called Green Living Collective.

The purpose of the club is to help students reduce waste and live more sustainably in their daily lives. We plan to hold monthly workshops on topics such as cooking with leftovers, repairing clothes, and saving energy in dorm rooms. We would also like to organize a clothing swap at the end of each semester.

I believe the club would benefit students in several ways. Many students want to live more sustainably but do not know where to start, and our activities would give them practical skills while also helping them save money. So far, twenty-three students have signed up to join.

Could you please tell me what documents are required to register the club and whether we need a faculty advisor?

Sincerely,
Liam O'Connor
explanation: 目的（活動内容を 具体的に） → 学生への 利点（実用性・節約） → 手続きの 質問。参加予定人数など 数字を 入れると 説得力が ある。（文体：フォーマル）

passage: The campus dining hall has started closing at 7 p.m. instead of 9 p.m. Many students with evening classes are unhappy. You decide to write to the dining services manager.
question:
Write an email in about 7 minutes. In your email, do the following:
• Explain the problem
• Describe how it affects students like you
• Request a change
Write as much as you can and in complete sentences.
answer:
Dear Dining Services Manager,

I am writing about the recent change to the dining hall's closing time from 9 p.m. to 7 p.m.

I understand that there may be good reasons for this decision, but it has caused problems for many students. I have a lab class every Monday and Wednesday from 5 p.m. to 7:30 p.m., so by the time I finish, the dining hall is already closed. I have a meal plan, but I now have to spend extra money on food from convenience stores.

Several of my classmates are in the same situation, and some of them have started skipping dinner.

Would it be possible to keep the dining hall open until 9 p.m. at least on weekdays, or to offer a simple takeaway option for students with evening classes?

Thank you for considering this request.

Sincerely,
Noah Green
